extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys, agents), and USPTO filing personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting Application Data Sheets (ADS), supplemental ADS, inventor oaths/declarations, and related filing data (priority, assignee, representative, venue/seal, and inventorship rules) for U.S. patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-suggested drawing figure on ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Office will use the drawing figure suggested by the applicant for the front page of the patent application publication when the suggestion is included on a compliant ADS timely filed before the process of publishing the application begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office is not bound by the applicant’s figure suggestion; failure to use the suggested figure will not be considered a material mistake for purposes of corrected publication under 37 CFR 1.221(b). See Applicant-Suggested Drawing Figure in the Publication of Patent Applications, 1514 OG 107 (September 5, 2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent—Latin name and variety denomination
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b)(3) requests that the plant patent applicant state the Latin name and the variety denomination for the plant claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Latin name and variety denomination are usually included in the specification and will be included in any plant patent or publication if included in an ADS or data sheet; inclusion aids the UPOV database compilation and makes that process more efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative information in ADS (registration/customer number)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative information includes the registration number appointed with a power of attorney in the application (preferably by reference to a customer number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS does not constitute a power of attorney in the application (pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b)(4) and pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.32), because the Office does not expect the ADS to be executed by the party who may appoint a power of attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority/continuity data in ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic priority information should include the application number (series code and serial number), the filing date, the status (including patent number if available), and relationship of each application for which a benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS constitutes the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C.119(e) or 120 and complies with 37 CFR 1.78(a)(3)/(d)(3); if included in the ADS, a specific reference does not otherwise have to be made in the specification (e.g., first sentence). Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b)(5) does not apply to provisional applications. If continuity data is in the ADS but not in the specification, the patent front page will take the continuity data from the ADS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority information in ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign priority information in the ADS should include the application number, country, and filing date of each foreign application for which priority is claimed, as well as any foreign application having a filing date before that of the application for which priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS constitutes the claim for priority as required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b) and 37 CFR 1.55. The statute does not require any particular form for claiming benefit of a prior foreign application. Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b)(6) does not apply to provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee information in ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b)(7) provides that assignee information includes the name (person or juristic entity) and address of the assignee of the entire right, title, and interest in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of assignee information in the ADS does not substitute for compliance with any requirement to have an assignment recorded by the Office (37 CFR part 3). Providing assignee information in the ADS is considered a request to include such information on the patent application publication. Assignment recording is required for legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental ADS cannot correct certain items
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental application data sheet may be supplied prior to payment of the issue fee to correct or update information in a previously submitted ADS or an oath or declaration under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.67.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental ADS cannot be used to correct the following: (1) inventorship changes (37 CFR 1.48); (2) correspondence changes (pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.33(a)); and (3) citizenship changes (pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63 or pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.67). Supplemental ADSs must be titled 'Supplemental Application Data Sheet' and contain all seven section headings listed in 37 CFR 1.76(b) with appropriate data for each heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form requirements for supplemental ADS (pre-Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before September 16, 2012, a supplemental ADS must be titled 'Supplemental Application Data Sheet' (variations accepted), be a full replacement copy of the original ADS with each of the seven section headings listed in pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(b) and all appropriate data, be submitted with all changes indicated, and be signed as it is a paper or amendment filed in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes should preferably be shown with insertions/underlining and deletions by strike-through or brackets. Any ADS submitted after the filing date is a supplemental ADS regardless of whether an original ADS was submitted on filing. If ADS is used to correct data shown in an oath/declaration, it should show original incorrect info with strike-through/brackets and new info underlined to ensure the patent will reflect the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: If no original ADS filed, first ADS must be titled 'Supplemental'
rubrics_metrics.description: If no ADS was originally filed, but applicant wants to submit an ADS to correct, modify, or augment the original application data, the ADS, even though it is the first-filed ADS, must be titled 'Supplemental Application Data Sheet.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ADS submitted after filing is treated as a supplemental ADS; titles like 'Supp. ADS' or 'Supplemental ADS' are accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS governs inconsistencies; latest submitted information controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution of inconsistent information supplied by both an ADS and other documents (e.g., the oath or declaration) is addressed in pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(d): if an ADS is inconsistent with information provided in another document submitted at the same time or previously, the ADS will control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(d)(1) provides that the latest submitted information will govern notwithstanding whether supplied by an ADS, an amendment, correspondence, or an oath/declaration, except as provided by pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(d)(3). Because ADS is intended as the means by which applicants provide most information, when another document has more accurate information than a concurrently supplied ADS (37 CFR 1.76(d)(2)), a supplemental ADS should be submitted to conform the ADS to the correct information.

rubrics_metrics.name: When oath/declaration governs inventors and citizenship (1.76(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(d)(3), the oath or declaration under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63 or pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.67 governs inconsistencies with the ADS in the naming of inventors and setting forth their citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If different inventors are listed in the ADS than in the oath/declaration, the inventors named in the oath/declaration are considered the inventors named in the patent application. Any change in inventorship set forth in the oath/declaration must be by way of a request under 37 CFR 1.48(a). If citizenship is incorrectly set in the oath/declaration, the inventor must submit a supplemental oath or declaration under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.67 with correct citizenship notwithstanding correct identification in the ADS. A supplemental ADS cannot be used to correct the citizenship error in the oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting residence vs citizenship vs name spelling errors
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ADS improperly identifies an inventor's residence and an executed declaration sets forth the correct but different residence, the Office will capture the residence found in the ADS. Applicant should submit a supplemental ADS with the corrected residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the spelling of the inventor’s name is incorrect, a request under 37 CFR 1.48(f) is required. If an application is filed with ADS correctly setting forth citizenship and an executed declaration sets forth different incorrect citizenship, the Office will capture the citizenship found in the ADS, but applicant must still submit a supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 by the inventor setting forth the correct citizenship. If the error is one of residence, no change would be required (pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(d)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office reliance on ADS even when statute/rule indicates oath governs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will rely upon information supplied in the ADS over an oath or declaration to capture data even where the type of information supplied (citizenship, inventorship) is governed by the oath or declaration according to statute (pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 115) or rule (pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.41(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the oath/declaration contains correct information and the ADS does not, the information in the ADS must be corrected by submission of a request for correction and a supplemental ADS. Spelling errors of inventors' names still require 37 CFR 1.48(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class/subclass and Art Unit identification in ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of class/subclass information in the ADS permits applicants to aid in identification of the appropriate Art Unit to examine the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may decline to honor an applicant’s identification/request if internal staffing/workload requires handling by a different Art Unit; honoring every request could lead to forum shopping. Where the art or claims encompass areas of expertise of more than one Art Unit, reassignment may occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant authority when applicant is not inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant is not an inventor, the applicant information should include the applicant’s authority to apply for the patent on behalf of the inventor (see pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.42, 1.43 and 1.47).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: if inventor is deceased or legally incapacitated, include 'Legal Representative' as the authority; if a petition under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47(b) is filed, authority is 'Party in Interest under 35 U.S.C. 118'; if filed by Administrator of NASA, authority is 'Government Property Interest.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence indicated by Customer Number
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence information may be indicated by reference to a Customer Number to which correspondence is to be directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PCT or PLT model international forms in lieu of ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective December 18, 2013, 37 CFR 1.76 was amended to permit use of Patent Law Treaty Model International Forms or the Patent Cooperation Treaty Request Form in lieu of an ADS under 37 CFR 1.76 as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 601.05(a), subsection IV, for more information; PCT/PLT forms may substitute when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-authorized declarations in lieu of oaths (35 U.S.C. 25 and 37 CFR 1.68)
rubrics_metrics.description: By statute the Director may prescribe that any document required to be under oath may be subscribed to by a written declaration in such form as prescribed; 37 CFR 1.68 permits a written declaration in lieu of an oath provided the declarant is warned that willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a declaration is used, the declarant must set forth that statements of own knowledge are true and statements made on information and belief are believed to be true. A 37 CFR 1.68 declaration need not be ribboned to other papers even if signed in a foreign country but must be maintained with the application. Statutory declarations under 28 U.S.C. 1746 are acceptable if they otherwise comply with law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies vs originals of oaths/declarations and authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy (photocopy or facsimile) of an originally executed oath or declaration is encouraged to be filed as applications are maintained electronically; the original should be retained by applicant or representative as evidence of authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a question of authenticity arises, the USPTO may require submission of the original. See 37 CFR 1.4(d)(1)(ii). Office personnel are authorized to accept statutory declarations under 28 U.S.C. 1746 in lieu of an 'oath' or declaration under 35 U.S.C. 25 and 37 CFR 1.68 if compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may administer oaths and jurisdictional limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or affirmation may be made before any person within the United States authorized by law to administer oaths; an oath in a foreign country may be made before diplomatic/consular officers of the United States authorized to administer oaths, or per 37 CFR 1.66.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military personnel authority is set forth in 10 U.S.C. 1044(a). Attorneys acting as notaries are not barred by the language of statutes provided local law permits it, but the District of Columbia prohibits an attorney in the case from administering the oath. If an oath is known to be void because administered by an attorney where invalid, a new oath/declaration should be submitted and the file may be referred to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seal requirements and proof of official character
rubrics_metrics.description: A seal is usually impressed on an oath; documents with seals cannot be adequately scanned, so the Office encourages declarations rather than oaths. Some oaths (military or certain states) need not be impressed with a seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the person before whom the oath is made is not provided with a seal, the official character must be established by competent evidence (certificate from a clerk of a court of record or other proper officer having a seal). Jurisdictions vary as to embossed vs rubber-stamped seals; the latter should not be confused with a stamped expiration date of the notary’s commission. See MPEP § 602.04 for foreign-executed oaths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue in oath/jurat must correspond with notary jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Venue (the portion indicating where the oath is taken) must correspond with the county and state in the seal; if venue and seal do not correspond, the jurisdiction of the notary must be determined from statements by the notary appearing on the oath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venue and notary jurisdiction must correspond or the oath is improper. The oath should show on its face that it was taken within the jurisdiction of the certifying officer or notary; otherwise submit a new oath/declaration or a certificate of the notary that the oath was taken within his/her jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor naming and oath/declaration requirements (37 CFR 1.41 and MPEP §602.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must include, or be amended to include, the name of the inventor for any invention claimed in the application. For nonprovisional applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, inventorship is the inventor(s) set forth in the ADS filed before or concurrently with the inventor’s oath/declaration; if no ADS is filed before or concurrently, inventorship is that set forth in the inventor’s oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once an ADS or the inventor’s oath/declaration is filed in a nonprovisional application, any correction of inventorship must be pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48. For provisional applications, inventorship is set forth in the prescribed cover sheet (37 CFR 1.51(c)(1)); corrections must be pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48. If neither ADS nor oath/declaration is filed, inventorship is as set in application papers filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b)/(c) unless applicant supplies names with the processing fee. Applicants planning to name inventors in an ADS should ensure the ADS is signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.33(b) and present on filing or at least before filing the inventor’s oath/declaration; otherwise the oath/declaration may control. For international applications entering national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, inventorship is as set in ADS filed with the 371 submission; the inventor’s oath/declaration cannot be used to name inventors in that context.
